output.brief: FCR fell because of the Finance credit-limit change on 14 April, not mainly the new starters. The in-call credit limit dropped from £100 to £25, and larger adjustments now go automatically to the Billing Resolution team. Billing calls referred rose from 7% to 54% in the same week. Referred calls resolve at about 33% and non-referred at about 82%, and both rates are unchanged. Billing FCR fell from 79% to 56%. The April intake's referral rate (56%) matches tenured staff (53–54%). Tenured agents' FCR fell by the same amount (75% to 67%). The tariff mix shift is small, and tariff FCR held at 85%. The IVR change on 28 April doesn't fit the timing, since the drop was already complete by 21 April. Performance plans for the new starters would punish the wrong group, so don't do that. Next step: agree a revised credit limit with Finance, backed by post-call sampling of credits, and trial it on two teams for six weeks. Track FCR and the unsupported-credit rate. The Financial Controller has said she'd accept a trial like this. Don't restore the old limit everywhere at once. The audit concern is real. Confidence is fairly high. The complaints link is only an association.
